taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-10, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 104.3 | 6.31 | 6.31
2 | 416.7 | 17.57 | 23.88
3 | 264.5 | 2.29 | 26.17
4 | 856.9 | 2.63 | 28.80
5 | 641.5 | 26.88 | 55.68
6 | 7698.1 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KHKH-type.

Is this label correct for these layer values? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"label_correct": true or false, "curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine if the label KHKH is correct, we evaluate the sequence of resistivities for each group of three consecutive layers:

1.  **Layers 1-2-3:** $104.3 < 416.7 > 264.5$. This follows the pattern $r_1 < r_2 > r_3$, which corresponds to **K**.
2.  **Layers 2-3-4:** $416.7 > 264.5 < 856.9$. This follows the pattern $r_2 > r_3 < r_4$, which corresponds to **H**.
3.  **Layers 3-4-5:** $264.5 < 856.9 > 641.5$. This follows the pattern $r_3 < r_4 > r_5$, which corresponds to **K**.
4.  **Layers 4-5-6:** $856.9 > 641.5 < 7698.1$. This follows the pattern $r_4 > r_5 < r_6$, which corresponds to **H**.

Combining these, the curve type is KHKH.

{"label_correct": true, "curve_type": "KHKH"}
